why: The dashboard aggregates look clean (0 5xx, canary p95 95ms vs stable 96ms, flat over all four 30s windows), but the raw log shows a tail regression that only exists in version 1.1. Facts (each one is a claim below): (1) 18 of 729 canary /search requests took more than 200ms, while 0 of 2273 stable /search requests did. (2) Those slow canary responses cluster tightly at 633-656ms, versus a canary /search median of 47ms and a stable /search maximum of 193ms. (3) They are not errors: 0 5xx and 0 non-200 responses in the whole test, and every slow canary /search request returned 200. (4) They are spread across the entire run, from t=3.2s to t=113.3s, 18 occurrences. (5) The effect is confined to /search: canary /browse had 0 requests over 200ms and canary /checkout had 1, while stable /checkout itself had 7. Judgement: fact 1 plus fact 5 mean this is a version-specific regression on one endpoint, not load noise or a shared-infrastructure blip, because the stable pods served 3x the traffic on the same endpoint in the same window with no request anywhere near that range; fact 4 rules out a cold-start/warm-up artifact; fact 2 means the affected users wait ~13x the normal search time, which is customer-visible even though fact 3 means nothing fails outright. Judgement: at 25% traffic this surfaces as ~2.5% of canary searches; promoting to 100% would apply the same regression to all search traffic, and the aggregate p95 would keep hiding it. The cost of waiting is one blocked release, so I rollback and hand the ~640ms stall on /search to the owning team as the thing to fix before the next canary.
